::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
## TL;DR

A $5'\times 5'$ agricultural census and a $96\times 144$ Earth system model grid differ by a factor of 675 in cell count, so the census must be regridded before the two can be combined. Crop production in the census is a per-cell total, in tonnes, and that decides the method: `terra::resample(..., method = "sum")` adds every fine cell's tonnes into the coarse cell that contains it and conserves the global total, while bilinear interpolation, the usual default, would return coarse values about 675 times too small. In R, `ncdf4` extracts the production layer, `terra` regrids it, and `ggplot2` shows both grids for a visual check. You also get the rule for which method each kind of field needs.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Corrected, October 2026

An earlier version of this page regridded the production layer with bilinear interpolation. Production is a total per cell, and bilinear interpolation reads only the few fine cells nearest each coarse-cell centre, so the regridded values were roughly $1/675$ of the coarse-cell totals. The code now uses `terra::resample(method = "sum")`, which conserves the total; the regridded map made with the old code has been removed.
:::

## Resolution mismatch

Global atmospheric chemistry and climate models (e.g., CESM, GEOS-Chem) simulate biogeochemical cycles on coarse Eulerian grid meshes—typically $1.9^\circ \text{ latitude} \times 2.5^\circ \text{ longitude}$ (or $2^\circ \times 2.5^\circ$). Conversely, observational agricultural inventories and satellite-derived land-use datasets are archived at fine spatial scales ($5' \times 5'$, approximately $10\text{ km}\times 10\text{ km}$ at the equator).

Direct point sampling of fine datasets onto model grids introduces spatial aliasing and numerical artifacts. A systematic regridding pipeline must preserve spatial gradients and account for spherical coordinate boundaries.

| Attribute | Source Dataset (Agricultural Census) | Target Model Grid (CESM / GEOS-Chem) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Spatial Resolution** | $5\text{ arc-minutes}$ ($1/12^\circ \approx 0.0833^\circ$) | $1.9^\circ\text{ lat} \times 2.5^\circ\text{ lon}$ ($f19\_f19$ configuration) |
| **Grid Dimensions** | $4320 \times 2160$ cells ($9.33 \times 10^6$ nodes) | $144 \times 96$ cells ($1.38 \times 10^4$ nodes) |
| **Data Reduction Factor** | $1.0\times$ (Raw resolution) | $\approx 675\times$ spatial compression |

### Bilinear spatial interpolation

Bilinear interpolation is the right tool for a smooth field defined at points, such as temperature, and the wrong one for this census. For an arbitrary target grid center $(\lambda, \phi)$ bounded by four adjacent source nodes $Q_{11}=(\lambda_1, \phi_1)$, $Q_{12}=(\lambda_1, \phi_2)$, $Q_{21}=(\lambda_2, \phi_1)$, and $Q_{22}=(\lambda_2, \phi_2)$, bilinear interpolation computes the target value $f(\lambda, \phi)$ via two successive 1D linear interpolations:

$$f(\lambda, \phi) = \frac{1}{(\lambda_2 - \lambda_1)(\phi_2 - \phi_1)} \begin{bmatrix} \lambda_2 - \lambda & \lambda - \lambda_1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} f(Q_{11}) & f(Q_{12}) \\ f(Q_{21}) & f(Q_{22}) \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \phi_2 - \phi \\ \phi - \phi_1 \end{bmatrix}$$

### Spherical cell area and mass diagnostics

When regridding extensive variables (such as total crop production in metric tons), total global mass must be conserved across transformations:

$$M_{\text{total}} = \sum_{i,j} \rho(\lambda_i, \phi_j) \cdot A(\lambda_i, \phi_j)$$

where the spherical surface area of grid cell $(\lambda_i, \phi_j)$ with angular bounds $[\lambda_w, \lambda_e]$ and $[\phi_s, \phi_n]$ is:

$$A(\lambda_i, \phi_j) = R_{\text{Earth}}^2 \cdot (\lambda_e - \lambda_w) \cdot (\sin\phi_n - \sin\phi_s)$$

The census stores production as a total per cell, $\rho A$ already multiplied out. Bilinear interpolation treats each stored number as a value at a point and reads four of them at each coarse-cell centre, so a coarse cell receives roughly one fine cell's tonnes instead of the sum of the 675 it covers. A per-cell total has to be regridded by summing.

## Regridding workflow

### Step 1: Environment setup and NetCDF ingestion

```r
library(ncdf4)      # NetCDF low-level interface
library(terra)      # Raster construction and resampling
library(reshape2)   # Matrix to long-format dataframe conversion
library(tidyverse)  # Tidyverse data pipelines and ggplot2
```

```r
# Open the NetCDF handle and inspect dimensions
nc_name <- "maize_AreaYieldProduction.nc"
nc <- nc_open(filename = nc_name)

# Extract spatial coordinates and production matrix (layer 6 = production)
lon_source <- ncvar_get(nc = nc, varid = "longitude")
lat_source <- ncvar_get(nc = nc, varid = "latitude")
raw_matrix <- ncvar_get(nc = nc, varid = "maizeData")[, , 6]

nc_close(nc)
rm(nc)

# Assign explicit coordinate dimnames to prevent longitude inversion
dimnames(raw_matrix) <- list(lon = lon_source, lat = lat_source)
df_source <- melt(raw_matrix)

head(df_source, 4)
```

### Step 2: Source and target raster construction

```r
# Convert the coordinate-value table into a source raster.
# Values are maize production in tonnes per 5' cell: a per-cell total.
r_source <- rast(df_source, type = "xyz", crs = "EPSG:4326")

# Target climate model grid: 96 x 144 cells over the globe.
# 96 rows over 180 degrees is 1.875 degrees, close to CESM's f19 grid.
nlat_target <- 96
nlon_target <- 144
r_target <- rast(nrows = nlat_target, ncols = nlon_target, crs = "EPSG:4326")
```

### Step 3: Sum the totals onto the coarse grid

```r
# Production is a per-cell total, so add the tonnes of every 5' cell into the
# coarse cell that contains it. method = "sum" weights each source cell by the
# fraction of it inside the target cell, so the global total is conserved.
# Bilinear interpolation would read a few nearby 5' cells at each coarse-cell
# centre and return values about 675 times too small.
r_regridded <- resample(r_source, r_target, method = "sum")

# Check: the global total must be unchanged
c(source = global(r_source, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]],
  regridded = global(r_regridded, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]])

# Back to a (lon, lat, value) table; xy = TRUE gives each cell's centre
df_regridded <- as.data.frame(r_regridded, xy = TRUE)
names(df_regridded) <- c("lon", "lat", "value")
```

### Step 4: Spatial distribution check

```r
# Plot high-resolution source dataset
plot_source <- df_source %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = value)) +
  geom_raster(interpolate = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_b(na.value = NA, name = "Production") +
  borders(colour = "white", size = 0.2) +
  coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Source Data: High-Resolution Maize Production (5' x 5')", x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")

plot_source
```

![Source High-Resolution Grid](unnamed-chunk-5-1.png)

```r
# Plot regridded coarse model dataset
plot_regridded <- df_regridded %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = value)) +
  geom_raster(interpolate = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_b(na.value = NA, name = "Production (t)") +
  borders(colour = "white", size = 0.2) +
  coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Regridded Data: Climate Model Mesh (96 x 144)", x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")

plot_regridded
```

The regridded map that appeared here was made with the earlier bilinear code and showed per-cell values far too small, so it has been removed. Running the corrected code above on the census file regenerates it, with each coarse cell holding the summed tonnes of the fine cells it covers.

### Production R pipeline module

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## View Modular Production Code (`regrid_netcdf_raster.R`)

```r
#' Spatial Regridding Module for Agricultural NetCDF Datasets
#'
#' @param nc_path Path to input NetCDF file.
#' @param var_name Variable identifier in NetCDF.
#' @param layer_idx Specific slice index for 3D/4D arrays.
#' @param nlat,nlon Rows and columns of the global target grid.
#' @param method "sum" for per-cell totals such as production or harvested area;
#'   "average" for densities and fractions; "bilinear" only for smooth intensive
#'   fields such as temperature.
#' @return Dataframe with coordinates (lon, lat) of cell centres and regridded values.
regrid_crop_data <- function(nc_path, var_name, layer_idx = 1, nlat = 96, nlon = 144, method = "sum") {
  if (!file.exists(nc_path)) {
    stop(paste("File not found:", nc_path))
  }

  nc_handle <- ncdf4::nc_open(nc_path)
  on.exit(ncdf4::nc_close(nc_handle), add = TRUE)

  lons <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc_handle, "longitude")
  lats <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc_handle, "latitude")
  data_array <- ncdf4::ncvar_get(nc_handle, var_name)

  if (length(dim(data_array)) == 3) {
    data_matrix <- data_array[, , layer_idx]
  } else {
    data_matrix <- data_array
  }

  dimnames(data_matrix) <- list(lon = lons, lat = lats)
  r_src <- terra::rast(reshape2::melt(data_matrix), type = "xyz", crs = "EPSG:4326")
  r_tgt <- terra::rast(nrows = nlat, ncols = nlon, crs = "EPSG:4326")

  r_out <- terra::resample(r_src, r_tgt, method = method)
  out <- terra::as.data.frame(r_out, xy = TRUE)
  names(out) <- c("lon", "lat", "value")
  out
}
```
:::

### Data and code availability

- **Dependencies**: R $\ge 4.0.0$, `ncdf4`, `terra`, `reshape2`, `tidyverse`, `ggplot2`.
- **Dataset**: Global Crop Yield and Production NetCDF repository (Monfreda et al., University of Minnesota / McGill University).

## Resampling method tradeoffs

| Resampling Method | Algorithmic Mechanism | Mass Conservation | Recommended Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nearest Neighbor** | Assigns nearest grid center value | Poor (discontinuous step jumps) | Discrete categorical fields (e.g. USDA plant functional types, soil taxonomy classes). |
| **Bilinear Interpolation** | Distance-weighted 4-node interpolation | Approximate (smoothing at boundaries) | Continuous physical variables (temperature, relative humidity, crop yield indices). |
| **First-Order Conservative** | Overlapping polygon area-weighted sum | Exact ($100\%$ mass conserved) | Extensive mass variables (total harvested production, nitrogen fertilizer mass, regional emissions). |

## Key takeaways

- A 5-arc-minute census grid has about 675 times as many cells as a $1.9^\circ \times 2.5^\circ$ model grid; regridding is a large reduction, not a relabelling.
- Ask what each stored number is before choosing a method. Production in tonnes is a total per cell; regrid it with `terra::resample(r, s, method = "sum")`, which conserves the global total. Bilinear interpolation would return values about 675 times too small.
- Use `method = "average"` for densities and fractions, and bilinear only for smooth intensive fields such as temperature.
- Assign `dimnames` before melting, build the source raster with `rast(df, type = "xyz")`, and read results back with `as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE)`, which returns exact cell centres.
- Compare the global total before and after regridding; it is one line and catches a wrong method immediately.
- Plot source and target side by side on the same colour scale before trusting the output.
